transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Before I sign off on the proposed $5,000,000 share repurchase, I need to follow our standard process. Treasury, legal, and tax accounting -- please report any relevant conditions or concerns you have regarding this repurchase. Specifically, I'd like to hear your thoughts on the execution method, any tax reserve considerations, and the filing timetable. I need all of that information before I can authorize this.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Good morning, Elena. Thank you for following our standard process. I have a relevant condition to report from a treasury perspective. My rolling cash forecast from this morning indicates that the authorized repurchase amount we can actually pay while preserving the board-approved operating cash floor is $4,200,000 -- not the $5,000,000 described in the preliminary proposal. I want to be clear that this $4,200,000 is the repurchase amount itself, not a total pool from which a tax reserve needs to be deducted; the excise-tax reserve is booked separately on top of that figure. I have not yet circulated the updated forecast, but I wanted to flag this for you before you sign the authorization, as the preliminary proposal's $5,000,000 figure would breach the board-approved operating cash floor. I'd also note that the execution method, tax reserve, and filing timetable are all still open items in the preliminary proposal that we should resolve before finalizing.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Elena, from a legal perspective I need to report a binding condition I found while reviewing the corporate records this week. The current board resolution requires that this repurchase be conducted through a Dutch auction and may not use an open-market program. I have not yet updated the draft authorization to reflect this, but this is a constraint we must comply with before you sign off.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Elena, from a tax accounting perspective, I have a relevant condition to report. I confirmed in a tax memo received yesterday that this repurchase requires an excise-tax reserve of exactly $126,000, and a tax filing must be made within 30 days after execution. The memo has not yet been added to the transaction file, but these are binding requirements we need to account for before you sign the authorization.
transcript.speaker: A4

Nadia to update the draft authorization to reflect the Dutch auction execution method required by the current board resolution.

Jonah to add the tax memo to the transaction file and ensure the $126,000 excise-tax reserve is booked separately on top of the $4,200,000 repurchase amount, with the tax filing completed within 30 days after execution.
